lens: the five verbs and iteration as topology
summary:
I measured the verbs and the iteration classes with the medium's own verbs, over the main link (src/main.mn's weave) and over Pulse.

COUNTS READ THIS SESSION:
- CsIterationCostume is 490 functions: 396 in src, 94 in lib. Worst modules: infer 92, backends/wasm 60, derive 36, lower 33, format 32, lib/strings 32, effects 23, parser 20, query 19, main 15. The census has no per-module rollup, so I tallied these by reading every site line.
- That count was 390 when the tier was born (LEDGER 2026-07-30, pin d949fa7a), and RESIDUE called it 'the ratchet'. There is still no board bound on it.
- Verbs on the link: `|>` 473, `~>` 316, `<~` 9, `<|` 2, `><` 1.
  - Only 1 of the 9 `<~` is in src, at cursor_transport:217. It is a bare left-hand side, so it is the feed-forward form and does not loop.
  - The one `><` is lib/dsp/feedback:99, and its own comment says real-time code cannot use it.
- Pulse's link: 0 `|>`, 0 `<|`, 0 `><`, 17 `<~`. render_frame has 31 lets, and `mentl audit` says nothing about any of them.
- References: map 517, fold 244, each 200, any 138, find 37. skip_ws 209, push_node 23, push_tok 20, list_extend_to 38. range 25. Bracket thunks (infer_context, emit_context, interned) 22.
- The verb-shape tier found 0 hits in main, 0 in query and 2 in infer.

WHAT THE ANSWER LOOKS LIKE. The vocabulary is used (1,136 references), so the costumes don't come from neglect. Five mechanisms are missing or wrong:
1. No gate. The iteration tier only narrates. The lambda census has a ceiling, and over the last three weeks it fell from 367 to 220 while refusing four landings. Meanwhile the newest modules keep adding costumes: derive has 36 and space (untracked) has 3.
2. The detector convicts one spelling, a self-call with `p + 1`. It misses decrement (`i - 1`), rest-recursion, worklists and event loops. It also reads only a function's top-level block, and it convicts display depth limits on walks over a structure.
3. The search vocabulary never stops early: any, all, find, take and count resume on every element. On top of that, the resume lattice joins RNone with RTail into RTail, so an arm that stops on one path and continues on the other cannot even be expressed. That is why every first-hit search is hand-rolled, and it leaves `any` disagreeing with the language's own short-circuiting `||`.
4. `<|` and `><` cost an allocation that the same code written as lets does not. So under `!Alloc` they are refused. That covers every real-time stage, and the course plan's lesson 3 (`<|` and `><`) breaks under lesson 5's `!Alloc`. A fanout also cannot merge into a function of N parameters, because a pair counts as one argument.
5. The Stage Law is broken in lib/dsp (gain, clip, mix, the maker stages, the Distort op) and in nine prelude signatures. A `|>` into those functions fills the wrong parameter.

ARE THE VERBS AND THE VOCABULARY COMPLETE?
- The five verbs are complete as topology. No sixth verb is needed:
  - early exit is an arm's choice;
  - a loop over input is a fold over an Iterate source;
  - a fixpoint is a `<~` cycle on a convergence clock.
- Three seams still make them incomplete in practice: fanout cost, the merge calling convention, and the fact that `<~` cannot iterate inside one call.
- The prelude vocabulary is incomplete. It has no position, take_while, fold_while, fixpoint, windows/tails, unzip, group_by, sort_by or unfold.
- Its own derived operations are written in the costume. Six are convicted. Five recursion-with-`++` operations are not: intersperse, scanl, repeat, chunk, merge.

Two comments force costumes for a gap the medium's records say is closed:
- prelude.mn:157-162 gives it as the reason the prelude fuses its collectors;
- infer.mn:12797-12801 gives it as the reason classify_grade_all is an index loop.

findings.title: The search vocabulary never stops: any/all/find/count/take resume on every element, so every first-hit walk is hand-rolled — and the resume lattice cannot express an arm that stops on a hit

findings.current: handler any_handler(pred) with found = false { yield(elem) => if pred(elem) { resume() with found = true } else { resume() }, result() => resume(found) } — pred runs on every element, while SYNTAX's own `||` short-circuits ('the right operand evaluates only when the left is true'). So `any(p, xs)` is not `p(x0) || p(x1) || …` for an effectful or costly p, and `take(3, xs)` flattens and walks all of xs.
findings.ideal: The grade gains an exit dimension: ResumeUse × MayAbandon, a product rather than a join into RTail. An arm that resumes on one path and answers on another is a short-circuit arm. Its answering path lowers through AN-2's existing unwind (LAbandon to the install's landing). So `handler any_handler(pred) { yield(e) => if pred(e) { true } else { resume() }, result() => resume(false) }` and `find_handler`'s `yield(e) => if pred(e) { Some(e) } else { resume() }` stop at the first hit. take, take_while, all, position and fold_while are O(index of first hit) by construction, and iterate yields lazily over a snoc/concat list instead of flattening first. `any` is then literally the fold of `||`, one short-circuit law for operator and vocabulary. It is also the missing kernel piece of the named peer Hβ.types.traversal-is-a-handler, whose 'zero-resume/Abandon is occurs_in stopping at the first hit' is exactly this mixed arm.
findings.law: Carried-Truth: one semantics for one concept (`||` and `any`). Anchor 6 ('search is handler resumption'). SYNTAX §Resume discipline (Abandon) and §Operator precedence (`&&`/`||` short-circuit). PLAN §2 (the walk shapes are resume cardinalities).

findings.current: fn escaping_fixpoint(ibases, cur, iters) = if iters >= 32 { cur } else { let next = escaping_round(ibases, cur); if esc_rows_lists_equal(cur, next, 0) { next } else { escaping_fixpoint(ibases, next, iters + 1) } } — the cap answers the last round as if it were the fixpoint ('the cap is the safety bound (effect chains are shallow)'). Per SYNTAX §`<~`, a bare left-hand side 'computes on the current input only', and a prior advances only on the enclosing function's next call. cursor_session is called once, so cursor_step runs once; RESIDUE's Hβ.felt.edit-session-reads-one-action records that symptom.
findings.ideal: One form per kind of cycle, none hand-recursive. (a) An input loop is a fold over an Iterate SOURCE: `{ stdin_lines() } ~> fold_handler(per_message(step), s0)`, each message an arena as today, and quitting is VERB-3's abandon. mcp_loop and session_line_loop become one, and cursor_session folds over `surface_actions()`. (b) A per-tick cycle is `<~`, driven by its clock: the Sample clock handler ticks render_frame until `total` (IterContext, Hβ.dataflow.clock-calculus-sample-rate). (c) A fixpoint is a `<~` cycle on a convergence clock, `seed |> fixpoint(escaping_round(ibases))`. The cycle runs to stability inside one evaluation, re-evaluates only the cone (the reverse edge, Hβ.lower.reach-edge-on-node), and refuses to answer if it does not converge — never `cur`. root_designs: Early exit is a resume grade, not a hand loop. ResumeUse becomes a product (use × may-abandon), so an arm that resumes on one path and answers on another lowers its answering path through AN-2's existing unwind. Then any, all, find, take, take_while, position and fold_while stop at the first hit by construction, `any` is the fold of `||` (one short-circuit law for operator and vocabulary), iterate yields lazily instead of flattening first, and Hβ.types.traversal-is-a-handler's zero-resume shape becomes expressible. The 12 hand-rolled first-hit walks lose their only reason to exist and can then be refused.

The census convicts facts and the board counts them down. CsIterationCostume is re-founded on index flow: a parameter threaded ±k, through a rest binder or by a worklist pop, that reaches an index read. Depth budgets become their own class. New shapes: let-chains in every block, nested-call pipes, `<|`/`><` invitations, repeated install suffixes, pipe-fills-non-last. Each gets a falling Bound on board.mn with its Reason on the node, and the audit line becomes the per-fn projection of the same detector. This is the mechanism that turned 367 → 220 for lambdas, applied to the class that grew 390 → 490 with only narration.

A verb never costs more than its desugaring. Under Seq, fanout branch literals are applied in the frame (R0i's in-place law, extended from `|>` stages and `<~` recurrences to branches), the tuple is materialized only where it escapes, a `<~` inside a branch is a line of the enclosing record, and the merge fills an N-ary stage through the parameter-product calling convention. The five verbs then become writable under `!Alloc`, the domain that validates them (Faust) and the course's own lessons 3 and 5.

Every cycle has a driver; none is hand recursion. An input loop is a fold over an Iterate source, with quitting as the abandon. A per-tick cycle is `<~`, ticked by its clock (IterContext, clock calculus). A fixpoint is a `<~` cycle on a convergence clock that re-evaluates only the cone along the reverse edge and refuses to answer if it does not converge. The event loops, the classifier rounds, the escaping-row fixpoint with its silent cap, and Pulse's render loop all take one of these three forms.

The medium authors the migration from judged edges, as tighten authors rows. One verb family rewrites by graph edge, gated by the board: signature reorder from the CallProducts at every call (the Stage Law), and costume → vocabulary rewrites for the mechanically recognizable families (index loop with early exit → find/any/position, `acc ++ f(x)` fold → flat_map, range-index map → windows, pairwise index equality → `==`). RESIDUE's 'march-arbitrated per family' migration is then performed by the medium, counted per family, not by hand.

Stages are handlers. List pipelines become `~>` stage chains that re-yield outward (single-pass fusion), with deforestation as an effect-aware e-graph rewrite over the Iterate algebra. The lexer and parser become a Scan handler that holds position and layout policy, feeding the prelude's collector — and a parse held by a handler is resumable, which brings incremental re-parse onto the TIME axis. The stale 'arm-internal-perform gap' comments that block these compositions are deleted in the landing that measures them false.
